description: Estimate the maximum home price you can afford using the classic 28/36 debt-to-income rule with your income, debts and down payment.

faqs.a: The 28/36 rule: housing costs should be at most 28% of gross monthly income (front-end), and all debts including housing at most 36% (back-end). This calculator uses the lower of the two.

Your maximum monthly housing payment is the smaller of 28% of gross monthly income and (36% of gross monthly income minus your other monthly debts). That payment is converted to a loan amount, then the down payment is added.
faqs.q: How is the affordable price calculated?

faqs.a: This is a principal-and-interest estimate only. Real lenders add taxes, insurance, HOA and PMI, which reduce what you can afford.
faqs.q: Does this include property taxes and insurance?

howto: Enter your gross annual income and current monthly debt payments.
Add your down payment, expected rate and loan term.
Read your maximum affordable home price and monthly payment.
